bears_on: Scope item 2 on #58 - whether the contention route is a defect or an accepted limit. A daemon that holds while any core is free, and drops a client's frame only when the machine is oversubscribed twice over, is arguably behaving reasonably. That is the owner's call and this supplies the number it needs rather than making it.

levels.note: blocks disagree; not demonstrable against 0.5x, p = 0.478

means: The contention lever needs the machine oversubscribed roughly 2x. Below full core saturation nothing fails at all - 0 of 32 across idle, 0.25x and 0.5x. At exactly 1x the effect is 2 of 12 and is NOT demonstrable against 0.5x (p = 0.478), and its two blocks disagree, 2 of 6 then 0 of 6. At 2x it is 8 of 18 with three blocks agreeing, p = 0.010 against 0.5x.
method_note: The 1x level is why this was run in blocks. Its first block read 2 of 6, which at n=6 would have been published as the threshold; the second read 0 of 6. That is windows-desk's finding on #57 applied prospectively rather than in hindsight - a 2-of-6 that becomes 2-of-12 was never an effect.
not_claimed: A sharp threshold. The data are consistent with a gradual rise between 1x and 2x and cannot resolve one - 2x against 1x is p = 0.235. Only 'nothing below saturation, clearly present at 2x' is supported.
